20: "Chure me! Chure—chure—chure! [2] A spell against the spell-weaver—may the evil tongue die of thirst, may the black eye burst. To him Karachoun [death], to me chure-perechure!"
18: Peredonov's face bore an expression of terror. He caught the glass which Volodin had filled and flung the vodka on to the floor, shouting:
17: "How is it, Ardalyon Borisitch, that you're not afraid to drink vodka when he pours it out? Perhaps he's exorcising it—don't you see his lips moving?"
16: Volodin said nothing, and preserving his injured look began to pour the vodka from the decanter into the glasses. Varvara said sarcastically:
15: "Don't pay any attention to him, Pavel Vassilyevitch," said Varvara consolingly. "He's only talking, his heart doesn't know what his tongue blabs."
14: "Take a drink, Pavloushka, and pour me one too," said Peredonov.
12: "If you have such an idea about me, Ardalyon Borisitch, then I can only say one thing: I thank you most humbly. If you think that way about me, what have I to say? What shall I understand by this, in what sense?"
11: "Any fool can do you harm," said Peredonov dejectedly. Volodin thrust out an offended lip, shook his head and said:
10: Peredonov became depressed. Varvara said sneeringly: "You've made a big enough fool of yourself, Ardalyon Borisitch. How can he do you any injury?"
9: "Ardalyon Borisitch, I have no idea of injuring you, and I don't want your sugar-candy because I don't like it."
8: Volodin laughed, but immediately afterwards looked hurt and said:
7: "Listen, Pavloushka," he said, "if you'll stop trying to injure me, then I'll buy you a pound of the best sugar-candy every week—you can suck it to my good health."
5: And Peredonov thought that he would get Volodin on his side.
3: "Why has he got evil intentions against me?" thought Peredonov. "What does he want?"
